name: Current test switch with shorting contact
summary: Panel test switch for CT circuits that shorts the CT side before opening the relay side, with a test jack between.
description: Panel-mounted test switches used in North American practice often combine a knife switch with a shorting contact for each CT circuit. Opening the switch first shorts the CT secondary and then isolates the relay or meter, so a test set can be connected without exposing the CT to an open circuit.

Current test switches are usually grouped with potential test switches and trip-isolating switches on one assembly. The symbol shows a single pole, and the full assembly arrangement, including which poles are current and which are potential, must be read from the panel wiring diagram.
readingNotes: Confirm the shorting contact is on the CT side.
Read the switch sequence for the assembly.
distinction: A current test switch shorts the CT on opening; a potential test switch simply opens the voltage circuit.
